newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE'S BUCHWA IRON MINE THROWN LIFELINE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE'S BUCHWA IRON MINE THROWN LIFELINE.

text.p: One of Zimbabwe's leading iron ore miners, Buchwa Mining Company, on the verge of closing down due to reduced reserves of high grade ore, has been thrown a lifeline by a proposed iron beneficiation project between Zimbabwe and Mozambique.

Buchwa general manager Charles Castelin said the mine was scaling down its operations due to dwindling resources of high grade ore when it was approached by South African mining house, JCI Limited, to participate in a proposed Z$6 billion iron ore project in Zimbabwe and Mozambique.

The project envisages that JCI, together with Buchwa, will mine and beneficiate lower grade iron ore in the Zimbabwean midlands and then rail it to the border where it will be reduced into hot briquetted iron (HBI) using natural gas from Mozambique.

The HBI, a particularly pure form of iron which can be mixed with scrap metal to produce high quality steel in electric arc furnaces, will then be exported to buyers in the Middle East and Pacific Rim via the port of Beira.

"The project is a very welcome development for Buchwa because it was going to close down because (state firm) Ziscosteel no longer needed iron ore from it," Industry and Commerce Minister Nathan Shamuyarira said recently at the Harare launch of a feasibility study into the project.

Castelin said Buchwa had already built up a dump of about 40 million tonnes of lower grade ore which used to be discarded as waste but this could be used as "feedstock" for the project if it proved viable.
